questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

__Many kitten is taught__ to hunt by their mothers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Many kittens are taught

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• If we look closely at the sentence, we can see that in the latter part of it, the phrase mentioned is *'their mothers'.*
 
• This implies that the subject of the sentence, that is, '*kitten'* should be plural, that is, *'kittens'*
 
• Also, since *'kittens' *is a countable noun, that is, one can count how many kittens are there at any instance, we use the quantifier *'many'. * *'Much' *is used for uncountable nouns like water, tea, etc.
 
• Further, since *'kittens' *is plural, we use the auxiliary verb *'are' *instead of *'is'*, which is a singular auxiliary verb

**
Thus the correct sentence is: *Many kittens are taught to hunt by their mothers.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

__
 
• A quantifier is a determiner or pronoun indicative of quantity (e.g. all, both )
 
• यदि हम वाक्य को करीब से देखते हैं, तो हम देख सकते हैं कि इसके उत्तरार्द्ध में, उल्लिखित वाक्यांश *'their mothers' हैं।*
 
• तात्पर्य यह है कि वाक्य का subject, 'kitten*'* plural होना चाहिए, अर्थात *'*Kittens*'.*
 
• इसके अलावा, चूंकि *'kittens'* एक countable noun है, इसलिए, कोई भी गिन सकता है कि किसी भी उदाहरण में कितने बिल्ली के बच्चे हैं, हम *'many' का उपयोग करते हैं।* *'Much'* का इस्तेमाल uncountable nouns जैसे water, tea आदि के लिए किया जाता है।
 
• इसके अलावा, *'kittens'* plural है, हम 'is**' के बजाय '**are** helping verb का उपयोग करेंगे​*,* जो एक singular helping verb है।

इस प्रकार सही वाक्य है: *Many kittens are taught to hunt by their mothers.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

India won the Border-Gavaskar Trophy in Australia.

options.text: The Border-Gavaskar Trophy is won by India in Australia.
The Border-Gavaskar Trophy was won by India in Australia.
India has won the Border-Gavaskar Trophy in Australia.
India has been won the Border-Gavaskar Trophy in Australia.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **The Border-Gavaskar Trophy was won by India in Australia.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The given sentence is in the active form and in the Simple past tense and we need to change it to the passive form.
 
• The Simple past tense in the active voice has the following form: **Subject + V2+ object**__
 
• The Simple past tense in the passive voice has the following form: __**Object+ was/were V3+ by + subject**__
 __
 
• Active:* I saved him.*
 
• Passive: * He was saved by me.*
 
 
 
• Rules of Conversion from Active to Passive Voice:
 
 
• Identify the subject, the verb, and the object.
 
• Change the object into the subject.
 
• Change the verb into the past participle form of the verb.
 
• Change the subject into an object.
 
 
 
• ​Therefore, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct Passive Voice:__ *The Border-Gavaskar Trophy was won by India in Australia.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. **

Seniors will hold the next meeting soon.

options.text: The next meeting will have been held by seniors soon.
Soon the next meeting would be held by seniors.
The next meeting will be hold by seniors soon.
The next meeting will be held by seniors soon.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4** 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• We can see that the given sentence is in **‘Future Indefinite Tense’** as the action is going to be done in the future **‘Soon’** and [**Will** + **‘Verb 1st form’ (hold)] **is used.
 
• In Passive voice:-
 
 
• **‘Future Indefinite Tense (Passive Voice)’**, we always use **‘Will be/Shall be’ **as a helping verb and **‘Verb 3rd form (past participle)’ **as a main verb.
 
• Start the sentence with "**the receiver of the action (Object) ***i.e.*** ‘the next meeting”.**
 
• Remember to use **the preposition ”by” to introduce the doer of the action (Subject)**. Here in the sentence,** the doer (subject) is ‘seniors’.**
 
 

According to the above instructions, **the final sentence would be** *‘The next meeting will be held by seniors soon.’*

 

**Note**: Both the Options 3rd and 4th are making the same sense but if we convert the given sentence into passive voice, then option 4 will be accurate grammatically.

 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Future Indefinite - Passive Voice - **[Object + will be/shall be + verb 3rd form + subject]**.

 
 
• I shall drive a car in the morning.
 
• *A car shall be driven by me in the morning.*
 
• Teachers will buy some chocolates for their students next week.
 
• *Some chocolates will be bought by teachers for their students next week.*

__
 
• The passage describes the youth of today.__
 
• Let's find out the usage of the words given in options-
 
 
• **Accord** means to give or grant someone (power, status, or recognition).
 
• **Origin** means the point or place where something begins, arises, or is derived.
 
• **Reservoir** means a supply or source of something.
 
• **Reference** means the use of a source of information in order to ascertain something.

questions.question: Which of these should be filled at (2) as per the context of the passage?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4 i.e. employ.**

 
• Let's find out the usage of the words given in options-
 
 
• **Consider** means think carefully about (something), typically before making a decision.
 
• **Interact** means act in such a way as to have an effect on each other.
 
• **Prepare** means make (something) ready for use or consideration.
 
• **Employ** means make use of.
